sources.title: MSMR · May 2026 full issue
sources.notes: Table 2 branch-year counts/rates extracted. PDF tables preferred over erroneous web chart alt text. Includes Coast Guard; Space Force separate from 2023.

sources.title: AFHSD · Cold injury, July 2020–June 2025
sources.notes: Figure 4 names 23 locations with ≥25 cases over five seasons. Exact five-season totals are stated for five locations only in the narrative; other totals remain null. Scope includes unspecified cold injuries.

sources.title: DoD · Heat Illness Report to Congress · November 2023
sources.notes: 2018–2022: 11,218 diagnoses at >230 locations. Missing DRSi reports are not the same as diagnoses absent from all surveillance. Appendix C contains modeled flag-day histories at 15 training locations.

sources.title: DCPH-A · Weather-related injury surveillance archive
sources.notes: Additional installation charts and provisional year-to-date series; not merged into annual MSMR counts.

sources.title: DCPH-A · April 2026 heat surveillance summary
sources.notes: Indexed report identified; PDF retrieval returned 502. No numeric rows imported. Installation chart excludes counts below 10.

sources.title: Japan FDMA · Heat illness ambulance transports, 2025
sources.notes: May 1–September 30, 2025. Table 4-2, PDF page 10. Ambulance transports for heat illness, not a count of severe heat stroke; prefecture capital coordinates are display anchors.

sources.title: India NCRB / Ministry of Earth Sciences · Recorded heat/sunstroke deaths
sources.notes: Annexure 1, August 20, 2025 parliamentary response. State rows extracted; union territories excluded from map. Zero means zero recorded deaths, not proof of no heat mortality.

sources.title: Maricopa County · 2025 heat-related deaths report
sources.notes: Table A: 2021–2025 deaths including heat-caused and heat-contributed deaths; includes nonresidents. County anchor, not individual death locations.

sources.title: Spain Ministry of Health · 2025 summer assessment
sources.notes: May 16–September 30, 2025. 25 confirmed heat-stroke deaths and 3,832 MoMo modeled heat-attributable deaths are distinct measures, not an underreporting ratio.

sources.title: Santé publique France · Summer 2025 bulletin
sources.notes: June 1–September 15, 2025: >5,700 modeled heat-attributable deaths and >24,000 iCanicule urgent-care contacts (hyperthermia, dehydration, hyponatremia). Not added as exact map counts.

sources.title: CDC Tracking · Heat and heat-related illness
sources.notes: ED visits, hospitalizations and death-certificate mortality. County coverage, suppression, denominators and available years depend on indicator. Nationwide extract not yet imported.

sources.title: CDC · Heat & Health Tracker
sources.notes: Heat exposure, health outcomes, and vulnerability are distinct layers. Follow source links to query its current data.

sources.title: Florida Environmental Public Health Tracking
sources.notes: Heat-related events with geographic identifiers. Suppressed and unavailable cells must remain missing; data not imported.

sources.title: EPA · Cold-related deaths technical documentation
sources.notes: Mortality methods and CDC WONDER provenance; civilian cold outcome data not yet extracted.

sources.title: NASA GIBS · Open geospatial imagery services
sources.notes: Satellite land-surface temperature is not ambient air temperature, WBGT, or illness incidence. No environmental surface is inferred from case counts.

sources.title: US Army · TB MED 507 · Heat stress control
sources.notes: Primary military heat-stress guidance. Atlas is retrospective and does not replace local WBGT measurements or operational guidance.

sources.title: US Army · TB MED 508 · Cold-weather injury prevention
sources.notes: Primary cold-weather guidance cited by the AFHSD surveillance report.

sources.title: Navy · Prevention and treatment of heat and cold stress injuries
sources.notes: 2007 technical manual cited by 2026 MSMR. Retain publication date; not represented as newly issued guidance.

sources.title: AFHSD · Exertional rhabdomyolysis, 2021–2025
sources.notes: Keep separate from heat exhaustion/heat stroke; co-occurrence precludes simply adding counts.

sources.title: AFHSD · Exertional hyponatremia, 2021–2025
sources.notes: Distinct outcome; not treated as another heat illness case in this atlas.

sources.title: Natural Earth · Admin-0 and Admin-1 boundaries, v5.1.2
sources.notes: Public-domain boundaries for Japanese prefectures, Indian states and Spain. Simplified for web display. De facto boundaries; no position on disputed territory is implied.

sources.title: U.S. Census Bureau · 2023 cartographic boundary file, counties (1:5m)
sources.notes: Maricopa County, Arizona polygon (GEOID 04013).

sources.title: DoD · Military Installations, Ranges, and Training Areas (MIRTA) boundaries
sources.notes: Authoritative DoD site boundaries for planning, via the Esri U.S. Federal Datasets mirror. Used to draw footprints and test display anchors. Footprints are context: AFHSD counts are by diagnosis/report location, not by fence line. No overseas sites.

sources.title: Statistics Bureau of Japan · Population estimates, 1 Oct 2024, Tables 2–3
sources.notes: Total and age-65+ population by prefecture (thousands). Denominator for transports per 100,000. Population date precedes the May–Sep 2025 transport window by seven months.

sources.title: Japan FDMA · 2025 heat illness report, Table 4-2 (age and severity)
sources.notes: Same table as the transport totals. Severity is the initial-diagnosis category at the hospital (death, severe, moderate, mild). Age 65+ is the FDMA 高齢者 group.

sources.title: Copernicus ERA5 reanalysis via Open-Meteo Historical Weather API
sources.notes: Daily 2 m max/min air temperature, ~25 km grid cell nearest each display anchor. Hersbach et al. (2020), CC BY 4.0. Context only: not WBGT, not exposure during training, and not a cause of any count.

sources.title: NASA GIBS · MODIS Terra monthly daytime land-surface temperature
sources.notes: WMTS tiles streamed from NASA at view time; not stored here. Surface (skin) temperature of the ground, not air temperature or heat stress.

sources.title: OpenFreeMap · OpenStreetMap vector basemap
sources.notes: Open-source vector tiles from OpenStreetMap data (ODbL). Basemap boundaries are cartographic context, not data.
